items.reason: Reached only through @bitwarden/cli 2026.6.0 (latest 2026.9.1 still pins node-forge 1.4.0), and no patched node-forge exists (<=1.4.0 affected). The advisory concerns RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification; the harness uses bw for vault reads. Re-decide when a patched node-forge or bitwarden release ships.

Reached only through fast-glob 3.3.3 -> micromatch 4.0.8 -> braces 3.0.3, and no patched braces exists (3.0.3 is the latest; the advisory covers all versions). The risk is stack exhaustion from deeply nested brace patterns; the harness passes glob patterns from its own file tools, so the worst case is a failed tool call in the agent's own process. Re-decide when a patched braces or micromatch ships.

Reached only through vitest 4.1.x, a devDependency that runs during local and CI test runs and is not shipped in @ouro.bot/cli or ouro.bot. The advisory concerns code injection through unauthenticated manual mock registration in the test runner; the only patched line is vitest 5.x, a major upgrade across the whole suite. Re-decide with the vitest 5 migration.

The advisory concerns a Windows backslash traversal past the mock redirect allowlist in the test runner; the only patched line is vitest 5.x, a major upgrade across the whole suite. Re-decide with the vitest 5 migration.

Reached only through @azure/identity 4.x (DefaultAzureCredential in the mailroom, which never runs the authorization code flow) and @microsoft/teams.apps 2.x (pinned to msal-node ^5, bot client-credential tokens only). The advisory affects only the auth_code flow (acquireTokenByCode), which neither path calls; the patched line is msal-node 7.1, two majors past what those SDKs accept. Re-decide when @azure/identity and teams.apps accept msal-node 7.
